# Overview

This R Markdown document implements the complete **GARCH-family econometric analysis** for Chapter 4 of the thesis.

The analysis proceeds in four stages:

1. **GARCH(1,1) parameter estimation** (baseline, no sentiment)
2. **GARCH-X(1,1) parameter estimation** (sentiment-augmented)
3. **IGARCH(1,1) parameter estimation**
4. **IGARCH-X(1,1) parameter estimation**

For each model, I conduct:

- In-sample estimation
- Walk-forward 1-step-ahead variance forecasting
- Residual diagnostics (Ljung–Box tests on standardized residuals)
- Export of parameters and forecast outputs for integration with the Python empirical notebook

---

## Output files (Imported by Python Notebook)

- `garch_params_from_r.csv` → Baseline GARCH parameters  
- `garchx_params_from_r.csv` → GARCH-X parameters  
- `igarch_params_from_r.csv` → IGARCH parameters  
- `igarchx_params_from_r.csv` → IGARCH-X parameters  
- `garch_family_oos_forecasts_from_r.csv` → All OOS forecasts  
- `garch_family_diagnostics_from_r.csv` → Model diagnostics

# Load and prepare data
```{r load-data}
# ---- Data path ----
DATA_PATH <- "../Data/final_data.csv"

# ---- Load ----
df <- readr::read_csv(DATA_PATH, show_col_types = FALSE)

# ---- Parse date (auto-detect common formats) ----
df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date, tryFormats = c("%d/%m/%Y", "%Y-%m-%d"))

if (any(is.na(df$Date))) {
  stop("Date parsing failed. Check the Date format in final_data.csv.")
}

# ---- Sort by date ----
df <- dplyr::arrange(df, Date)

# ---- Standardise sentiment column ----
if ("Trends" %in% names(df) && !"Search_Interest" %in% names(df)) {
  df <- dplyr::mutate(df, Search_Interest = Trends)
}

# ---- Log returns (percent) ----
df <- df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(r = 100 * (log(Close) - log(dplyr::lag(Close)))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(r))

# ---- Basic checks ----
stopifnot(!any(is.na(df$r)))
stopifnot(is.numeric(df$r))

# ---- Report ----
cat("Data loaded successfully.\n")
cat("Date range:", min(df$Date), "→", max(df$Date), "\n")
cat("Observations:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Columns:", paste(names(df), collapse = ", "), "\n\n")
```

# Section 1: GARCH and IGARCH model specifications

## Specify the models
```{r garch-family-spec}

# Extract return series (dependent variable)
r <- df$r

# =====================================================
# 1. Baseline GARCH(1,1)
# =====================================================
# Standard symmetric GARCH model
# Allows alpha + beta < 1 (mean-reverting variance)

spec_garch_norm <- rugarch::ugarchspec(
  variance.model = list(
    model = "sGARCH",
    garchOrder = c(1, 1)
  ),
  mean.model = list(
    armaOrder = c(0, 0),     # Constant mean
    include.mean = TRUE
  ),
  distribution.model = "norm"
)

spec_garch_std <- rugarch::ugarchspec(
  variance.model = list(
    model = "sGARCH",
    garchOrder = c(1, 1)
  ),
  mean.model = list(
    armaOrder = c(0, 0),
    include.mean = TRUE
  ),
  distribution.model = "std"   # Student-t innovations
)

# =====================================================
# 2. Baseline IGARCH(1,1)
# =====================================================
# Integrated GARCH:
# Imposes alpha + beta = 1 (unit persistence)

spec_igarch_norm <- rugarch::ugarchspec(
  variance.model = list(
    model = "iGARCH",
    garchOrder = c(1, 1)
  ),
  mean.model = list(
    armaOrder = c(0, 0),
    include.mean = TRUE
  ),
  distribution.model = "norm"
)

spec_igarch_std <- rugarch::ugarchspec(
  variance.model = list(
    model = "iGARCH",
    garchOrder = c(1, 1)
  ),
  mean.model = list(
    armaOrder = c(0, 0),
    include.mean = TRUE
  ),
  distribution.model = "std"
)

cat("Baseline GARCH and IGARCH specifications created.\n")

```
## Estimate the models
```{r garch-family-fit}

# =====================================================
# Estimate baseline GARCH and IGARCH models
# =====================================================
# Solver: "solnp" (robust for volatility models)
# Standard errors are computed by default

# -------------------------------
# 1. Baseline GARCH(1,1)
# -------------------------------

fit_garch_norm <- rugarch::ugarchfit(
  spec   = spec_garch_norm,
  data   = r,
  solver = "solnp"
)

fit_garch_std <- rugarch::ugarchfit(
  spec   = spec_garch_std,
  data   = r,
  solver = "solnp"
)

# -------------------------------
# 2. Baseline IGARCH(1,1)
# -------------------------------

fit_igarch_norm <- rugarch::ugarchfit(
  spec   = spec_igarch_norm,
  data   = r,
  solver = "solnp"
)

fit_igarch_std <- rugarch::ugarchfit(
  spec   = spec_igarch_std,
  data   = r,
  solver = "solnp"
)

cat("Baseline GARCH and IGARCH models fitted successfully.\n")
cat("Solver used: solnp\n\n")

```
## Extract and report the GARCH-family model parameters
```{r garch-family-params}

# =====================================================
# Extract parameter estimates with inference
# =====================================================
# Returns coefficient table (coef, SE, t, p)

extract_results <- function(fit, model_name) {
  
  mat <- fit@fit$matcoef
  
  out <- data.frame(
    param     = rownames(mat),
    coef      = mat[, 1],
    std_error = mat[, 2],
    t_value   = mat[, 3],
    p_value   = mat[, 4],
    model     = model_name,
    row.names = NULL
  )
  
  return(out)
}

# -------------------------------
# Extract coefficient tables
# -------------------------------

res_garch_norm  <- extract_results(fit_garch_norm,  "GARCH_Normal")
res_garch_std   <- extract_results(fit_garch_std,   "GARCH_Student_t")
res_igarch_norm <- extract_results(fit_igarch_norm, "IGARCH_Normal")
res_igarch_std  <- extract_results(fit_igarch_std,  "IGARCH_Student_t")

garch_family_params <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  res_garch_norm,
  res_garch_std,
  res_igarch_norm,
  res_igarch_std
)

# =====================================================
# Add model-level statistics
# =====================================================
# Log-likelihood, AIC, BIC for model comparison

model_stats <- data.frame(
  param = c("loglik", "AIC", "BIC"),
  model = rep(c(
    "GARCH_Normal",
    "GARCH_Student_t",
    "IGARCH_Normal",
    "IGARCH_Student_t"
  ), each = 3),
  coef = c(
    likelihood(fit_garch_norm),
    infocriteria(fit_garch_norm)[1],
    infocriteria(fit_garch_norm)[2],
    
    likelihood(fit_garch_std),
    infocriteria(fit_garch_std)[1],
    infocriteria(fit_garch_std)[2],
    
    likelihood(fit_igarch_norm),
    infocriteria(fit_igarch_norm)[1],
    infocriteria(fit_igarch_norm)[2],
    
    likelihood(fit_igarch_std),
    infocriteria(fit_igarch_std)[1],
    infocriteria(fit_igarch_std)[2]
  ),
  std_error = NA,
  t_value   = NA,
  p_value   = NA
)

garch_family_params <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  garch_family_params,
  model_stats
)

# =====================================================
# Export
# =====================================================

dir.create("garch_family", showWarnings = FALSE)

readr::write_csv(
  garch_family_params,
  "garch_family/garch_family_params_from_r.csv"
)

cat("✓ Saved: garch_family/garch_family_params_from_r.csv\n")

```

# Section 2: GARCH-family models estimation with sentiment
## Prepare external regressors
```{r garchx-prep}

# =====================================================
# Prepare external regressor for GARCH-X / IGARCH-X
# =====================================================
# Sentiment proxy: Google Trends search interest
# Entering the conditional variance equation

stopifnot("Search_Interest" %in% names(df))

# Extract sentiment series
x_sent_raw <- df$Search_Interest

# Ensure no missing values
stopifnot(!any(is.na(x_sent_raw)))

# Convert to matrix (required by rugarch)
x_sent <- as.matrix(x_sent_raw)

# Standardise for numerical stability (mean 0, sd 1)
x_sent <- scale(x_sent)

# Sanity checks
stopifnot(nrow(x_sent) == length(r))

cat("External regressor prepared.\n")
cat("Observations:", nrow(x_sent), "\n\n")

summary(as.numeric(x_sent))

```

## Specify the GARCH-X family models
```{r garchx-spec}

# =====================================================
# Specify sentiment-augmented GARCH models (GARCH-X)
# =====================================================
# External regressor enters the conditional variance:
#   h_t = omega + alpha*e_{t-1}^2 + beta*h_{t-1} + gamma*Sentiment_t

# -------------------------------
# 1. GARCH-X(1,1)
# -------------------------------

spec_garchx_norm <- rugarch::ugarchspec(
  variance.model = list(
    model = "sGARCH",
    garchOrder = c(1, 1),
    external.regressors = x_sent
  ),
  mean.model = list(
    armaOrder = c(0, 0),
    include.mean = TRUE
  ),
  distribution.model = "norm"
)

spec_garchx_std <- rugarch::ugarchspec(
  variance.model = list(
    model = "sGARCH",
    garchOrder = c(1, 1),
    external.regressors = x_sent
  ),
  mean.model = list(
    armaOrder = c(0, 0),
    include.mean = TRUE
  ),
  distribution.model = "std"
)

# =====================================================
# Specify sentiment-augmented IGARCH models (IGARCH-X)
# =====================================================
# IGARCH imposes alpha + beta = 1 (unit persistence)

spec_igarchx_norm <- rugarch::ugarchspec(
  variance.model = list(
    model = "iGARCH",
    garchOrder = c(1, 1),
    external.regressors = x_sent
  ),
  mean.model = list(
    armaOrder = c(0, 0),
    include.mean = TRUE
  ),
  distribution.model = "norm"
)

spec_igarchx_std <- rugarch::ugarchspec(
  variance.model = list(
    model = "iGARCH",
    garchOrder = c(1, 1),
    external.regressors = x_sent
  ),
  mean.model = list(
    armaOrder = c(0, 0),
    include.mean = TRUE
  ),
  distribution.model = "std"
)

cat("GARCH-X and IGARCH-X specifications created.\n")
```

# Section 3: Walk-Forward Forecasting

## Settings (must match Python notebook)

```{r forecast-settings}

# =====================================================
# Walk-forward forecasting configuration
# =====================================================
# These settings MUST match the Python notebook
# Forecast evaluation follows the OOS design
# described in the research proposal (2017–2025 sample)

# ---- Forecast split ----
TEST_SIZE <- 0.20          # 20% out-of-sample
ROLLING_WINDOW <- 750      # Set to NA for expanding window
LAGS <- c(10, 20)          # Used later for diagnostics / features

# ---- Sample size ----
N <- nrow(df)

# ---- Compute split index ----
split_idx <- floor((1 - TEST_SIZE) * N)
n_oos <- N - split_idx

# ---- OOS dates ----
oos_dates <- df$Date[(split_idx + 1):N]

# ---- Report ----
cat("Forecast settings:\n")
cat("  Test size:", TEST_SIZE, "\n")
cat("  Rolling window:", ROLLING_WINDOW, "\n")
cat("  In-sample size:", split_idx, "\n")
cat("  Out-of-sample size:", n_oos, "\n")
cat("  OOS period:", 
    as.character(min(oos_dates)), "→", 
    as.character(max(oos_dates)), "\n\n")
```
## 1-Step Variance Forecast Function

```{r forecast-function}

# =====================================================
# 1-step ahead conditional variance forecast
# =====================================================
# Re-estimates model at each step using either:
#   - Expanding window
#   - Rolling window
# Returns: h_{t|t-1} = sigma^2 forecast

one_step_var_forecast <- function(
  spec,
  t_idx,
  use_external = FALSE,
  window_length = NULL
) {
  
  # ---- Define estimation window ----
  end_est <- t_idx - 1
  
  if (is.null(window_length) || is.na(window_length)) {
    start_est <- 1                     # Expanding window
  } else {
    start_est <- max(1, end_est - window_length + 1)  # Rolling window
  }
  
  r_est <- df$r[start_est:end_est]
  
  # =====================================================
  # Re-estimate model on window
  # =====================================================
  
  if (use_external) {
    
    x_est <- as.matrix(df$Search_Interest[start_est:end_est])
    x_next <- matrix(df$Search_Interest[t_idx], nrow = 1)
    
    # Update spec with window-specific external regressor
    spec@model$variance.external.regressors <- x_est
    
    fit <- rugarch::ugarchfit(
      spec   = spec,
      data   = r_est,
      solver = "solnp"
    )
    
    fc <- rugarch::ugarchforecast(
      fit,
      n.ahead = 1,
      external.forecasts = list(vregfor = x_next)
    )
    
  } else {
    
    fit <- rugarch::ugarchfit(
      spec   = spec,
      data   = r_est,
      solver = "solnp"
    )
    
    fc <- rugarch::ugarchforecast(
      fit,
      n.ahead = 1
    )
  }
  
  # Return conditional variance forecast
  return(as.numeric(rugarch::sigma(fc))^2)
}

cat("Forecast function defined.\n\n")

```
## Generate walk-forward forecasts (GARCH family)

```{r forecast-generate}

# =====================================================
# Initialize forecast storage
# =====================================================

# ---- Baseline GARCH ----
f_garch_norm  <- numeric(n_oos)
f_garch_std   <- numeric(n_oos)

# ---- GARCH-X ----
f_garchx_norm <- numeric(n_oos)
f_garchx_std  <- numeric(n_oos)

# ---- Baseline IGARCH ----
f_igarch_norm <- numeric(n_oos)
f_igarch_std  <- numeric(n_oos)

# ---- IGARCH-X ----
f_igarchx_norm <- numeric(n_oos)
f_igarchx_std  <- numeric(n_oos)


# =====================================================
# Walk-forward forecasting loop
# =====================================================

cat("Generating walk-forward forecasts...\n")

idx_forecast <- (split_idx + 1):N

for (i in seq_along(idx_forecast)) {
  
  t_idx <- idx_forecast[i]
  
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # 1. GARCH baseline
  # -------------------------------------------------
  
  f_garch_norm[i] <- one_step_var_forecast(
    spec_garch_norm,
    t_idx,
    use_external = FALSE,
    window_length = ROLLING_WINDOW
  )
  
  f_garch_std[i] <- one_step_var_forecast(
    spec_garch_std,
    t_idx,
    use_external = FALSE,
    window_length = ROLLING_WINDOW
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # 2. GARCH-X
  # -------------------------------------------------
  
  f_garchx_norm[i] <- one_step_var_forecast(
    spec_garchx_norm,
    t_idx,
    use_external = TRUE,
    window_length = ROLLING_WINDOW
  )
  
  f_garchx_std[i] <- one_step_var_forecast(
    spec_garchx_std,
    t_idx,
    use_external = TRUE,
    window_length = ROLLING_WINDOW
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # 3. IGARCH baseline
  # -------------------------------------------------
  
  f_igarch_norm[i] <- one_step_var_forecast(
    spec_igarch_norm,
    t_idx,
    use_external = FALSE,
    window_length = ROLLING_WINDOW
  )
  
  f_igarch_std[i] <- one_step_var_forecast(
    spec_igarch_std,
    t_idx,
    use_external = FALSE,
    window_length = ROLLING_WINDOW
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # 4. IGARCH-X
  # -------------------------------------------------
  
  f_igarchx_norm[i] <- one_step_var_forecast(
    spec_igarchx_norm,
    t_idx,
    use_external = TRUE,
    window_length = ROLLING_WINDOW
  )
  
  f_igarchx_std[i] <- one_step_var_forecast(
    spec_igarchx_std,
    t_idx,
    use_external = TRUE,
    window_length = ROLLING_WINDOW
  )
  
  # Progress indicator
  if (i %% 50 == 0) {
    cat("  Completed:", i, "of", n_oos, "\n")
  }
}

cat("✓ Walk-forward forecasts generated.\n\n")

```

# Section 4: Residual Diagnostics

## Ljung-Box Test Helper

```{r diagnostics-helper}

# =====================================================
# Ljung–Box residual diagnostics
# =====================================================
# Tests:
#   1) Serial correlation in standardized residuals
#   2) Remaining ARCH effects in squared residuals

ljung_box_diagnostics <- function(fit, lags = c(10, 20), model_name = "") {
  
  # ---- Extract standardized residuals ----
  z <- residuals(fit, standardize = TRUE)
  z <- as.numeric(z[is.finite(z)])
  
  n <- length(z)
  
  # Number of estimated parameters (for df adjustment)
  k <- length(coef(fit))
  
  # ---- Initialize results container ----
  out <- data.frame(
    lag = lags,
    lb_stat_resid = NA_real_,
    lb_pvalue_resid = NA_real_,
    lb_stat_sqresid = NA_real_,
    lb_pvalue_sqresid = NA_real_,
    Model = model_name
  )
  
  # ---- Compute Ljung–Box tests ----
  for (i in seq_along(lags)) {
    
    L <- min(lags[i], n - 1)  # Avoid lag > sample size
    
    # Adjust df for parameter estimation
    adj_df <- max(L - k, 1)
    
    # Residuals
    bt_resid <- Box.test(
      z,
      lag = L,
      type = "Ljung-Box",
      fitdf = k
    )
    
    out$lb_stat_resid[i]   <- unname(bt_resid$statistic)
    out$lb_pvalue_resid[i] <- unname(bt_resid$p.value)
    
    # Squared residuals
    bt_sqresid <- Box.test(
      z^2,
      lag = L,
      type = "Ljung-Box",
      fitdf = k
    )
    
    out$lb_stat_sqresid[i]   <- unname(bt_sqresid$statistic)
    out$lb_pvalue_sqresid[i] <- unname(bt_sqresid$p.value)
  }
  
  return(out)
}

cat("Ljung–Box diagnostics function defined.\n\n")
```
## GARCH-family Baseline Diagnostics

```{r diagnostics-baseline}

# =====================================================
# Baseline model diagnostics (GARCH & IGARCH)
# =====================================================

# ---- GARCH ----
diag_garch_norm <- ljung_box_diagnostics(
  fit_garch_norm,
  lags = LAGS,
  model_name = "GARCH_Normal"
)

diag_garch_std <- ljung_box_diagnostics(
  fit_garch_std,
  lags = LAGS,
  model_name = "GARCH_Student_t"
)

# ---- IGARCH ----
diag_igarch_norm <- ljung_box_diagnostics(
  fit_igarch_norm,
  lags = LAGS,
  model_name = "IGARCH_Normal"
)

diag_igarch_std <- ljung_box_diagnostics(
  fit_igarch_std,
  lags = LAGS,
  model_name = "IGARCH_Student_t"
)

# ---- Combine ----
diag_baseline <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  diag_garch_norm,
  diag_garch_std,
  diag_igarch_norm,
  diag_igarch_std
)

# ---- Display ----
cat("Baseline model diagnostics (Ljung–Box):\n\n")
print(diag_baseline)

# ---- Export ----
dir.create("garch_family", showWarnings = FALSE)

readr::write_csv(
  diag_baseline,
  "garch_family/garch_family_baseline_diagnostics_from_r.csv"
)

cat("\n✓ Saved: garch_family/garch_family_baseline_diagnostics_from_r.csv\n")
```
Ljung–Box tests on squared standardized residuals fail to reject the null of no remaining ARCH effects at conventional levels, indicating that the GARCH-family models adequately capture volatility clustering. Some residual autocorrelation remains at shorter lags, suggesting limited mean dynamics not fully absorbed by the ARMA(0,0) specification.

ARCH-LM
```{r}
# =====================================================
# ARCH-LM Tests (Remaining ARCH Effects)
# =====================================================

library(FinTS)

# Helper function
arch_lm_test <- function(fit, lags = 10, model_name = "") {
  
  # Extract standardized residuals
  z <- residuals(fit, standardize = TRUE)
  z <- as.numeric(z[is.finite(z)])
  
  # ARCH-LM test
  test <- FinTS::ArchTest(z, lags = lags)
  
  data.frame(
    Model = model_name,
    Lags = lags,
    ARCH_LM_Stat = as.numeric(test$statistic),
    P_Value = as.numeric(test$p.value)
  )
}

# -----------------------------------------------------
# Baseline models
# -----------------------------------------------------

arch_garch_norm  <- arch_lm_test(fit_garch_norm, 10, "GARCH_Normal")
arch_garch_std   <- arch_lm_test(fit_garch_std, 10, "GARCH_Student_t")
arch_igarch_norm <- arch_lm_test(fit_igarch_norm, 10, "IGARCH_Normal")
arch_igarch_std  <- arch_lm_test(fit_igarch_std, 10, "IGARCH_Student_t")

# -----------------------------------------------------
# Sentiment models
# -----------------------------------------------------

arch_garchx_norm  <- arch_lm_test(fit_garchx_norm, 10, "GARCHX_Normal")
arch_garchx_std   <- arch_lm_test(fit_garchx_std, 10, "GARCHX_Student_t")
arch_igarchx_norm <- arch_lm_test(fit_igarchx_norm, 10, "IGARCHX_Normal")
arch_igarchx_std  <- arch_lm_test(fit_igarchx_std, 10, "IGARCHX_Student_t")

# -----------------------------------------------------
# Combine results
# -----------------------------------------------------

archlm_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  arch_garch_norm,
  arch_garch_std,
  arch_igarch_norm,
  arch_igarch_std,
  arch_garchx_norm,
  arch_garchx_std,
  arch_igarchx_norm,
  arch_igarchx_std
)

print(archlm_results)

# -----------------------------------------------------
# Export to Python folder
# -----------------------------------------------------

dir.create("garch_family", showWarnings = FALSE)

readr::write_csv(
  archlm_results,
  "garch_family/garch_family_archlm_from_r.csv"
)

cat("✓ Saved: garch_family/garch_family_archlm_from_r.csv\n")
```
